# FluidStreamKit

> Swift 6 package (iOS 17+, zero dependencies) that renders streaming LLM responses at 80–150+ tokens/sec without dropped frames. Token deltas go into an actor-owned UTF-8 ring buffer. A CADisplayLink drains it once per frame into a single-pass parser (prose, <thinking>, <tool_call> JSON, code fences), and the result renders into a TextKit 2 text view, editing only the line being written.

Products: `FluidStreamUI` (what apps import), `FluidStreamCore` (buffer and frame clock), `FluidStreamParser` (pure-Swift parser). `import FluidStreamUI` alone is enough: it re-exports the other two, so never add `import FluidStreamCore` or `import FluidStreamParser` in app code.

## Integrate (SwiftUI)

```swift
import FluidStreamUI

@State private var session = StreamSession()

FluidStreamView(renderer: session.renderer)
    .task {
        await session.start { buffer in              // runs off the main actor
            for try await delta in textDeltas() {    // the app's SSE text stream
                try await buffer.append(delta)       // String, Data or [UInt8]; suspends when the buffer is full
            }
        }                                            // return = finished, throw = cancelled
    }
    .onDisappear { session.cancel() }
```

Required in the app's Info.plist for 120 Hz on iPhone: `CADisableMinimumFrameDurationOnPhone` = YES.

## Rules for generated code

- Do NOT bind streamed text to `@State`, `@Published` or `@Observable` properties that drive SwiftUI `Text`. Use `FluidStreamView` / `StreamSession`. `FluidStreamView.updateUIView` is empty on purpose.
- Do NOT read `StreamTextView.textView.layoutManager`: it silently switches to TextKit 1. Use `textLayoutManager`.
- Append chunks (a delta or a network read), never byte by byte: each `append` is an actor hop.
- Only one producer per `StreamSession`. A second concurrent `append` throws `StreamBufferError.concurrentProducer`. `start` only runs once per session.
- Call `session.cancel()` when the screen goes away.
- Anthropic Messages API: use the adapter in `Examples/AnthropicChat/Sources/AnthropicStreaming`. `MessagesStreamer.stream(_:into:)` inside `session.start`, with `StreamSession(parserConfiguration: MessagesTextBridge.parserConfiguration)`. It maps `thinking` and `tool_use` content blocks to typed blocks. Never put an API key in an app; relay the stream through your own backend.
- Accessibility is on by default (VoiceOver sentence announcements, Dynamic Type re-scaling). Don't post per-token `UIAccessibility` announcements yourself.
- Customize with `StreamSession(flushPolicy:bufferCapacity:theme:parserConfiguration:)`, `StreamTheme.standard()`, `ParserConfiguration(thinkingTag:toolCallTag:recognizesCodeFences:)` and `FlushPolicy(maxBytesPerFrame:catchUpFrames:idleFramesBeforePause:)`.
- Callbacks: `session.renderer.onToolCall = { json, isStructurallyComplete in }`, `FluidStreamView(renderer:onFollowingChanged:onScrollActivityChanged:)`.
- UIKit: `StreamTextView(renderer:)`, with `jumpToLatest()` and `isFollowing`.
- Replay without streaming: `StreamRenderer().apply(text:isFinal:)`.
- Tests run on macOS with `swift test`. Use `ManualFrameTicker` with `StreamSession(ticker:)` to drive frames deterministically.
